items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And the next thing we knew, somebody had gotten him, well it was mob connections, they had gotten him a record contract with Columbia, and they gave Mitch Miller the job of promoting him.

ctx.x: It’s a real skill to be able to write something that comes from really, if it was just played from the top of your head, to try to put that on paper.

Yeah, oh, yeah. So Joe was very well supported by those arrangements. They really, and he knew what to do with them. He had an instrument and an ability to sing and actually he was kind of bugged about getting locked into the image of being a blues singer, because he wanted to be a ballad singer. And he knew he could do it, and he felt that he had come into the world of being a singer kind of on the tail end of the time when those kind of singers were easily promoted and sold to the general public. So you know he…

him he was such a nice man, and kind of innocent. And I just heard this on the grapevine, I never discussed it with Tony, but I heard that he bought his contract away from these guys that originally backed him, and they charged him a nice taste, but they were willing to let him go because he was a nice guy. And then I think it was either hearing the Basie band or getting a chance to work opposite the Basie band, he realized that that was the kind of the background he would like to hear behind him. He liked it.…
